verses.text: Yahweh says: “Behold, I will raise up against Babylon, and against those who dwell in Lebkamai, a destroying wind.
I will send to Babylon strangers, who will winnow her. They will empty her land; for in the day of trouble they will be against her all around.
Against him who bends, let the archer bend his bow, also against him who lifts himself up in his coat of mail. Don’t spare her young men! Utterly destroy all her army!
They will fall down slain in the land of the Chaldeans, and thrust through in her streets.
For Israel is not forsaken, nor Judah, by his God, by Yahweh of Armies; though their land is full of guilt against the Holy One of Israel.
“Flee out of the middle of Babylon! Everyone save his own life! Don’t be cut off in her iniquity; for it is the time of Yahweh’s vengeance. He will render to her a recompense.
Babylon has been a golden cup in Yahweh’s hand, who made all the earth drunk. The nations have drunk of her wine; therefore the nations have gone mad.
Babylon has suddenly fallen and been destroyed! Wail for her! Take balm for her pain. Perhaps she may be healed.
“We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed. Forsake her, and let us each go into his own country; for her judgment reaches to heaven, and is lifted up even to the skies.
‘Yahweh has produced our righteousness: come, and let us declare in Zion the work of Yahweh our God.’

“Make the arrows sharp! Hold the shields firmly! Yahweh has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes, because his purpose is against Babylon, to destroy it; for it is the vengeance of Yahweh, the vengeance of his temple.

Set up a standard against the walls of Babylon! Make the watch strong! Set the watchmen, and prepare the ambushes; for Yahweh has both purposed and done that which he spoke concerning the inhabitants of Babylon.
You who dwell on many waters, abundant in treasures, your end has come, the measure of your covetousness.
Yahweh of Armies has sworn by himself, saying, ‘Surely I will fill you with men, as with the canker worm; and they will lift up a shout against you.’
“He has made the earth by his power. He has established the world by his wisdom. By his understanding he has stretched out the heavens.

When he utters his voice, there is a roar of waters in the heavens, and he causes the vapors to ascend from the ends of the earth. He makes lightning for the rain, and brings the wind out of his treasuries.
“Every man has become brutish without knowledge. Every goldsmith is disappointed by his image; for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.
They are vanity, a work of delusion. In the time of their visitation, they will perish.
The portion of Jacob is not like these, for he is the former of all things; including the tribe of his inheritance: Yahweh of Armies is his name.
“You are my battle ax and weapons of war. With you I will break the nations into pieces. With you I will destroy kingdoms.
With you I will break in pieces the horse and his rider.

With you I will break in pieces the chariot and him who rides therein. With you I will break in pieces man and woman. With you I will break in pieces the old man and the youth. With you I will break in pieces the young man and the virgin.
With you I will break in pieces the shepherd and his flock. With you I will break in pieces the farmer and his yoke. With you will I break in pieces governors and deputies.
“I will render to Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight,” says Yahweh.
“Behold, I am against you, destroying mountain,” says Yahweh, “which destroys all the earth. I will stretch out my hand on you, roll you down from the rocks, and will make you a burned mountain.
They shall not take cornerstone from you, nor a stone for foundations; but you will be desolate for ever,” says Yahweh.

“Set up a standard in the land! Blow the trumpet among the nations! Prepare the nations against her! Call together against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz! Appoint a marshal against her! Cause the horses to come up as the rough canker worm!
Prepare against her the nations, the kings of the Medes, its governors, and all its deputies, and all the land of their dominion!
The land trembles and is in pain; for the purposes of Yahweh against Babylon stand, to make the land of Babylon a desolation, without inhabitant.
The mighty men of Babylon have stopped fighting, they remain in their strongholds. Their might has failed. They have become as women. Her dwelling places are set on fire. Her bars are broken.
One runner will run to meet another, and one messenger to meet another, to show the king of Babylon that his city is taken on every quarter.
So the passages are seized. They have burned the reeds with fire. The men of war are frightened.”
For Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says: “The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time when it is trodden. Yet a little while, and the time of harvest shall come for her.”

“Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon has devoured me. He has crushed me. He has made me an empty vessel. He has, like a monster, swallowed me up. He has filled his mouth with my delicacies. He has cast me out.
May the violence done to me and to my flesh be on Babylon!” the inhabitant of Zion will say; and, “May my blood be on the inhabitants of Chaldea!” will Jerusalem say.
Therefore Yahweh says: “Behold, I will plead your cause, and take vengeance for you. I will dry up her sea, and make her fountain dry.
Babylon will become heaps, a dwelling place for jackals, an astonishment, and a hissing, without inhabitant.
They will roar together like young lions. They will growl as lions’ cubs.
When they are heated, I will make their feast, and I will make them drunk, that they may rejoice, and sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake up,” says Yahweh.
“I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with male goats.
“How Sheshach is taken! and the praise of the whole earth seized! How Babylon has become a desolation among the nations!
The sea has come up on Babylon. She is covered with the multitude of its waves.
Her cities have become a desolation, a dry land, and a desert, a land in which no man dwells, neither does any son of man pass by it.
I will execute judgment on Bel in Babylon, and I will bring out of his mouth that which he has swallowed up. The nations shall not flow any more to him. Yes, the wall of Babylon will fall.
“My people, go away from the middle of her, and each of you save yourselves from Yahweh’s fierce anger.

Don’t let your heart faint. Don’t fear for the news that will be heard in the land. For news will come one year, and after that in another year news will come, and violence in the land, ruler against ruler.
Therefore behold, the days come that I will execute judgment on the engraved images of Babylon; and her whole land will be confounded. All her slain will fall in the middle of her.
Then the heavens and the earth, and all that is therein, will sing for joy over Babylon; for the destroyers will come to her from the north,” says Yahweh.
“As Babylon has caused the slain of Israel to fall, so the slain of all the land will fall at Babylon.
You who have escaped the sword, go! Don’t stand still! Remember Yahweh from afar, and let Jerusalem come into your mind.”
“We are confounded, because we have heard reproach. Confusion has covered our faces, for strangers have come into the sanctuaries of Yahweh’s house.”
“Therefore behold, the days come,” says Yahweh, “that I will execute judgment on her engraved images; and through all her land the wounded will groan.
Though Babylon should mount up to the sky, and though she should fortify the height of her strength, yet destroyers will come to her from me,” says Yahweh.
“The sound of a cry comes from Babylon, and of great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans!
For Yahweh lays Babylon waste, and destroys out of her the great voice! Their waves roar like many waters. The noise of their voice is uttered.
For the destroyer has come on her, even on Babylon. Her mighty men are taken. Their bows are broken in pieces, for Yahweh is a God of recompenses. He will surely repay.
I will make her princes, her wise men, her governors, her deputies, and her mighty men drunk. They will sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake up,” says the King, whose name is Yahweh of Armies.

Yahweh of Armies says: “The wide walls of Babylon will be utterly overthrown. Her high gates will be burned with fire. The peoples will labor for vanity, and the nations for the fire; and they will be weary.”

The word which Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, when he went with Zedekiah the king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Now Seraiah was chief quartermaster.
Jeremiah wrote in a book all the evil that should come on Babylon, even all these words that are written concerning Babylon.
Jeremiah said to Seraiah, “When you come to Babylon, then see that you read all these words,
and say, ‘Yahweh, you have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off, that no one will dwell in it, neither man nor animal, but that it will be desolate forever.’
It shall be, when you have finished reading this book, that you shall bind a stone to it, and cast it into the middle of the Euphrates.
Then you shall say, ‘Thus will Babylon sink, and will not rise again because of the evil that I will bring on her; and they shall be weary.’” Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.

footnotes.content: The Lord raises a destroying wind against pride itself. How gently He speaks it—not in anger, but in the patient work of justice. Even empires that forget Him find His word coming for them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Strangers will winnow Babylon, just as grain is winnowed. There's a painful mercy in it—the chaff must be separated. What we build without the Lord becomes only heap and ash.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No mercy for the young men—it sounds hard until you remember Babylon held Judah captive, and mercy stayed silent then. The Lord's hand is just, and sometimes justice costs everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In the land she conquered, she falls. How the circle turns. The streets that once echoed her victory now hold her ruin. The Lord remembers what is hidden from man.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Israel and Judah forsaken? No. The Lord holds His people even when their land is full of guilt. This is the strange goodness—we are guilty, yet not orphaned. He is Yahweh of Armies, and His covenant holds.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Flee the middle of Babylon—it's a call to separation, to distance yourself from what will fall. How much sorrow could be spared if we listened sooner to the Lord's warning to leave what destroys.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A golden cup—beautiful to hold, but poison to drink. Babylon became the instrument of the Lord's wrath, making nations mad with her wine. What glitters is not always good; what intoxicates often destroys.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Suddenly fallen—as if overnight, what seemed eternal crumbles. They call for balm, for healing, but some wounds run too deep. The wages of pride come due in a moment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even those who loved her cannot heal her. Her judgment has risen to heaven itself—there is no human remedy for what God has decided. Sometimes we must simply leave, and grieve what could not be healed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord has brought forth righteousness—He has vindicated His people. Now Zion declares His work. There is a quiet joy in witnessing the Lord's faithfulness, in speaking what He has done.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord stirs the hearts of the Medes. This is not chance but purpose—He moves nations like pieces on a board. It is vengeance for His temple, for the desecration of what is holy. His own house cries out for Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Set up a standard against the walls—the signal of coming war. The Lord has both purposed and done; His word does not return empty. What He has spoken concerning Babylon will surely come to pass.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abundant in treasures, dwelling on many waters—yet the end comes. Wealth and safety are illusions when they rest on covetousness. The measure of greed is always fulfilled, and always empties into ruin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord has sworn by Himself—there is no higher oath. He will fill Babylon with men as numerous as canker worms, and they will shout against her. What He swears, He performs.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: By His power the earth was made, by His wisdom the world stands. He has stretched out the heavens by His understanding. How small all human schemes become when set against the One who speaks worlds into being.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When He utters His voice, waters roar in heaven. He commands the vapors and lightning and wind—all treasuries at His word. Every storm, every rain is His signature on the sky.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every man has become brutish without knowledge—we craft idols of gold and silver, pouring our hands into false gods. But there is no breath in them; they are empty, and we, empty with them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Vanity and delusion—works of human hands that perish in their visitation. The idols we trust will turn to dust, and we with them if we cling too long.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jacob's portion is not like these, for He is the former of all things. Yahweh of Armies holds His inheritance, His covenant people. We are not crafted by human hands but chosen, redeemed, known by name.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You are my battle ax and weapons of war—the Lord speaks to Cyrus, to His instrument. With you I will break the nations. Sometimes the Lord uses the unaware to accomplish His purposes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The horse and rider will be broken—symbol of strength and authority both shattered. No earthly power stands when the Lord sets His hand against it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Chariot and rider, man and woman, old and young—all categories of humanity will know His judgment. None are spared; none can hide from the work of His hand. Yet see how specific—He knows each one.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shepherd and flock, farmer and yoke, governors and deputies—the whole order of Babylon's rule will crumble. When the Lord breaks a nation, He breaks everything that holds it together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will render to Babylon all the evil they did in Zion—the Lord takes account of what they inflicted in His sight. There is a reckoning, and it is His to render.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Behold, I am against you, destroying mountain—Babylon thought itself immovable as a mountain, yet the Lord speaks Himself against it. He will roll it down from the rocks and make it a burned mountain, a warning to all who see.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No cornerstone will remain, no foundation stone—Babylon will be utterly desolate forever. Not one stone left for rebuilding, not one anchor for return. The Lord speaks finality into the ruins.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Set up a standard in the land, blow the trumpet—the call to arms for the Lord's instruments. Ararat, Minni, Ashkenaz, the kingdoms of the north, all summoned. The very geography moves at His word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The nations, the kings of the Medes, the governors—all their dominion rises to conquer Babylon. What once ruled now serves the purpose of its own destruction.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The land trembles—creation itself is stirred by the Lord's purpose. The land of Babylon will become a desolation, without inhabitant. When God acts, even the earth knows it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The mighty men have stopped fighting; their might has failed. They became as women—not as insult but as fact: all their strength evaporates when the Lord removes His hand. Her dwelling places burn, her bars break.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One runner meets another, messenger to messenger—the city falls so fast that news stumbles over itself trying to reach the king. He learns his city is taken on every quarter, all at once, nowhere left to turn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The passages are seized, the reeds burned with fire, the men of war frightened. In a moment, all order breaks. The tools of war become useless; courage becomes fear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Babylon is like a threshing floor when it is trodden—the grain separates, the chaff flies away. Yet a little while, and the harvest comes for her. She will be scattered, winnowed, and blown away.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Nebuchadnezzar has devoured Israel, crushed and emptied her, swallowed like a monster, cast out. These are the words of Zion, speaking her long pain. The victim now witnesses her oppressor's doom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: May the violence done to me be on Babylon—Zion and Jerusalem speak, and their cry rises. The blood spilled in captivity, the flesh torn, all is remembered. The Lord hears the cry of the afflicted.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will plead your cause and take vengeance—the Lord Himself steps forward as advocate. He will dry up her sea, make her fountain dry. What sustains her will be stripped away.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Babylon becomes heaps, a dwelling place for jackals, an astonishment and a hissing. Where once lay glory and power, now jackals cry. What men built becomes a horror to behold.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They roar together like young lions, growl as lion cubs—the sound of Babylon's destruction is like beasts crying in the ruins. The city becomes a wilderness where wild things prowl.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When they are heated with wine, the Lord will make a feast, make them drunk, so they sleep a perpetual sleep. In their revelry, death comes quietly. They will not wake.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will bring them down like lambs to slaughter, like rams with goats—Babylon's mighty will be led as defenseless beasts to their doom. All strength fails before the Lord's purpose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: How Sheshach is taken—this is code-name for Babylon, hiding her shame in cipher. The praise of the whole earth seized, and she becomes a desolation among the nations. The proud fall before all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sea comes up on Babylon, covers her with multitude of waves. Water, symbol of chaos, overwhelms what once seemed secure. The deep swallows what men built.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Her cities become desolation, a dry land, a desert where no man dwells. The silence is complete—no commerce, no crowds, no life. Only emptiness remains.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will execute judgment on Bel—the god Babylon worshipped. What she has swallowed will be brought out of his mouth. The wall of Babylon will fall, and the nations will no longer flow to her false god.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: My people, go away from the middle of her—the call to separation echoes again. Save yourselves from the fierce anger of the Lord. There is yet time to flee.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't let your heart faint; don't fear the news. Rumors will come—one year this, another year that, violence and rulers warring. Yet these are not the end; hold firm in the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The days come when I will execute judgment on the engraved images of Babylon. Her whole land will be confounded, her slain will fall in her midst. The idols and the kingdom fall together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The heavens and earth, and all that is therein, will sing for joy over Babylon. Creation itself rejoices at the fall of what destroys. The destroyers come from the north at His command.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: As Babylon caused the slain of Israel to fall, so the slain of all the land will fall at Babylon. What she sowed, she reaps. The measure she measured comes back to her.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You who have escaped the sword, go; don't stand still. Remember the Lord from afar; let Jerusalem come into your mind. There is a home to return to, a people to rejoin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We are confounded, we have heard reproach; confusion covers our faces because strangers entered the sanctuaries of the Lord's house. The desecration cuts deep—holy places profaned, the face of shame turned inward.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Behold, the days come when I will execute judgment on her engraved images, and through all her land the wounded will groan. Her idols fall, and the groans of the dying echo through her land.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Though Babylon mount up to the sky, though she fortify the height of her strength, yet destroyers come from Me. No height is high enough to escape the Lord's hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sound of a cry comes from Babylon, and of great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans. The voice of her ruin rises—there is no silence left, no peace, only the sound of breaking.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord lays Babylon waste, destroys the great voice out of her. Her waves roar like many waters, but the noise of her voice is uttered—all her power becomes only noise soon to be forgotten.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The destroyer has come on her, even on Babylon. Her mighty men taken, their bows broken—for the Lord is a God of recompenses and will surely repay. What is done in rebellion finds its answer in judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will make her princes, her wise men, her governors and deputies, her mighty men drunk. They will sleep a perpetual sleep, not wake—says the King, Yahweh of Armies. His is the final word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The wide walls of Babylon utterly overthrown, high gates burned with fire. The peoples labor for vanity, the nations for fire, and they are weary. All their work becomes ashes in her destruction.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah commanded Seraiah—note his name means 'the Lord is my prince'—when he went with Zedekiah to Babylon. This is historical anchor: the fourth year of Zedekiah's reign, and Seraiah was chief quartermaster, entrusted with burden of word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah wrote in a book all the evil that should come on Babylon. The word is fixed, written, sealed. What the Lord has spoken will not be unspoken.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When you come to Babylon, see that you read all these words. A faithful man carries the word into the enemy's stronghold, speaks it where it will not be welcomed. Courage is obedience in the place of danger.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh, You have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off so no one will dwell in it. The prayer and the prophecy are one—the Lord's word spoken by a trembling voice in a foreign palace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When you have finished reading, bind a stone to it and cast it into the middle of the Euphrates. The word is delivered; now the symbol—the book, weighted down, sinks into the river. Babylon will sink likewise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Thus will Babylon sink, and will not rise again because of the evil that I will bring on her. Readers today hear an echo here—that pride built on conquest, greed that swallows the weak, and denial of God does sink. Nations rise and fall. We watch and learn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
